correctness.rationale: Let k=ceil(log₂ℓ), P=2^k. Each ℓ-window has at most one hole index j+1≡0(mod P), while its nonhole symbols depend only on index mod P. For fixed starting residue i mod P, if both windows contain holes their valuations depend on q and q+Δ where Δ=(d+b−a)/P>0. The complete parity-pair set is {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)} for odd Δ and all four for even Δ, with each pattern attained on arbitrarily large integer q through congruence choices. Shifting d by 2P preserves all nonholes, hole positions and Δ parity; hence entire boundary sets agree for every d>=ℓ, not just eventually. At most 4 patterns per each of P residues give 4P bound. Independently compared direct substitution/valuation prefixes with residue formula and shift for ℓ<=12; those finite tests are secondary to the all-width proof.

originality.rationale: Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland introduce extended boundary sequences and prove broad automaticity, with different Thue–Morse, Fibonacci and Sturmian examples. Their inspected main result is weaker than pure periodicity for the canonical period-doubling word, uniform across all window widths and with an explicit linear period. Guo–Lü–Wen discuss ordinary width-one boundary sequences, and full text was unavailable; possible overlap for ℓ=1 is acknowledged, but the all-width theorem is not claimed as a consequence of an isolated width-one result.
residual_risks: The ordinary boundary article Guo–Lü–Wen was not inspected in full, could contain ℓ=1 instance or more.
An unindexed specialized combinatorics note could state equivalent all-width periodicity.
T_ℓ is a valid period, not claimed minimal; 4P is an upper bound not equality.

value.rationale: Extended boundary sets are a natural language-combinatorial invariant measuring all two-window endpoint pairs. Pure periodicity in separation of an aperiodic automatic word is a structural strengthening over mere 2-automaticity, and the theorem supplies a uniform exact construction and linear-size/period bounds for every width, rather than a sparse finite census.

final_claim: For the 0→01,1→00 period-doubling fixed point p_j=ν₂(j+1) mod2, for every ℓ>=1 and d>=ℓ the full set of ordered endpoint pairs of length-ℓ blocks at separation d is purely periodic from its first domain value with period T_ℓ=2^(1+ceil(log₂ℓ)); at most 4·2^ceil(log₂ℓ) distinct pairs per set.
limitations: Claim only the specific period-doubling word with indices starting at zero and separations d>=ℓ.
No automatic-word universality or least-period optimality.
